summary.goal: Enable users to send direct messages to specific agents via intuitive entry points (status bar clicks, @mentions) without fragmenting the messaging UX across too many surfaces.
summary.context:
Currently, messages exist in two places: the /channels/:id view (full-page) and the MessagingSidebar (right-side panel). The status bar shows agent avatars that can be clicked. The question is: where should DMs live, and how do they relate to channels?

Key tension: We want quick access to DM agents, but we don't want three separate messaging surfaces that confuse users about where to find conversations.
summary.problem_statement: User wants to click an agent in the status bar to send a direct message, but unclear where that conversation should live. Options range from inline bubbles, to DM channels in the existing channel infrastructure, to a unified approach.

approaches.name: DMs as Special Channels
approaches.description: Treat DMs as channels (e.g., #dm-{userId}-{agentId}). They appear in the channel list, use the same infrastructure, and clicking an agent in status bar navigates to or opens the DM channel in the sidebar.
pros: Unified model - all messages are channels
/channels view naturally supports DMs alongside public channels
Message history persisted and searchable in one place
cons: Channel list could get cluttered with many DM channels
Need to distinguish DM channels from group channels in UI
Extra navigation step (click agent -> opens channel)
approaches.ux_implication: Status bar agent click opens MessagingSidebar with DM channel selected

approaches.name: Inline Chat Bubbles
approaches.description: Clicking an agent in the status bar opens a small chat bubble/popover anchored to the avatar. Ephemeral, quick interactions without navigating away.
cons: Easy to lose context of ongoing conversations
approaches.ux_implication: Conversations happen in-place but harder to track long-term

approaches.name: Unified Inbox with DM Sections
approaches.description: The /channels view and MessagingSidebar both support a 'Direct Messages' section alongside 'Channels'. DMs are visually grouped but use the same underlying channel infrastructure.
pros: Clear separation between group channels and DMs
Status bar click scrolls to DM section in sidebar
cons: Need to add section headers to existing channel list
approaches.ux_implication: Status bar agent click: (1) opens sidebar if collapsed, (2) scrolls to DMs section, (3) selects/creates DM with that agent

summary.recommendation_rationale:
Approach C (Unified Inbox with DM Sections) provides the best balance:

1. NO additional messaging surface - reuses existing channels infrastructure
2. Clear UX - DMs grouped in their own section, not mixed with public channels
3. Consistent mental model - matches Slack/Discord patterns users know
4. Quick access - status bar click opens sidebar to DM section
5. History preserved - DMs are just channels, same persistence/search

The /channels view should also support this: show both public channels AND DMs. This answers the question 'should /channels support DMs?' - yes, as a dedicated section.

acceptance_criteria.description: ChannelList shows two sections: 'Channels' and 'Direct Messages'
Clicking agent avatar in status bar opens MessagingSidebar to DM with that agent
If no DM channel exists with agent, one is created on first message
DM channels appear in /channels view under 'Direct Messages' section
DM channel names show agent display name, not channel ID
Only show 'Direct Messages' section if user has any DM channels
MessagingSidebar remembers last selected channel across navigation
Status bar agent click when agent has pending question: opens DM and scrolls to question

out_of_scope: DM notifications/badges (handled by existing channel infrastructure)
Agent-initiated DMs to users (handled by existing question queue)

resolved_decisions.question: Should clicking an agent in status bar always open the sidebar?
resolved_decisions.rationale: Simplest UX - consistent behavior. Users expect clicking an agent to message them.

resolved_decisions.question: How to handle DM channels for agents that are no longer active?
resolved_decisions.rationale: Preserve conversation history. Mark with visual indicator (grayed out, 'offline' badge).

design_decisions.decision: DMs are channels, not a separate messaging surface
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids fragmentation. One mental model: everything is a channel. DMs are just 1:1 channels.

design_decisions.decision: Status bar agent click opens MessagingSidebar to DM
design_decisions.rationale: Quick access without adding new UI surfaces. Reuses existing sidebar infrastructure.

createDmChannel joins planner-core to the DM channel
DM channels tracked in dmChannels Map (userId -> agentId -> channelId)
